### Observed differences

- In the later window, the outgoing routing of activity A26 is even more concentrated on a single destination: about 97.5 in 100 observed outgoing transitions go to A27, up from about 95 in 100 in the earlier window. [DIR001]
- The rare alternative destinations differ between the windows: earlier, transitions from A26 went to A08 about 5 times (of 201 outgoing transitions), to A20 about twice, and once each to A01, A04 and A06; in the later window none of these were observed, while rare transitions went to A02 about twice (of 202) and once each to A31, A40 and A45. [DIR001]
- The overall size of the routing difference is very small (cosine dissimilarity about 0.0005), even though it exceeds the difference seen in about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled data. [DIR001]
- These rare shares rest on only one or a few observations each, so a single rare transition can appear in one window and not the other. [DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence
The evidence is insufficient to infer a structural change in the process. Only one item was found where about 0.44 are expected by chance in an unchanged process (89 units tested), and that item shows the dominant route A26 → A27 essentially unchanged, with the differences confined to rare transitions observed only once or twice, which sampling variation alone can explain. [DIR001]

message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

The evidence contains a single item: DIR001, a control-flow direction indicator for activity A26. It compares the distribution of outgoing transitions from A26 before vs after.

Before components (shares of outgoing transitions of A26):
- A27: ~0.95 (95%)
- A08: ~0.025 (2.5%)
- A20: ~0.01 (1%)
- A01, A04, A06: ~0.005 each (0.5% each)

After components:
- A27: ~0.975 (97.5%)
- A02: ~0.0099 (~1%)
- A40, A45, A31: ~0.005 each (~0.5% each)

So the dominant transition A26 → A27 remains dominant, slightly increased from about 95 in 100 to about 97.5 in 100. Several rare transitions observed before (A01, A04, A06, A08, A20) no longer appear in the after window, and several new rare transitions appear (A02, A31, A40, A45).

Support: 201 outgoing transitions before, 202 after. So the rare components are based on very few observations: A08 at 2.5% of 201 ≈ 5 transitions; A20 at 1% ≈ 2 transitions; A01, A04, A06 at 0.5% ≈ 1 transition each. After: A02 at ~1% of 202 ≈ 2 transitions; A40, A45, A31 at ~0.5% ≈ 1 transition each.

observed_change = 0.00053 (cosine dissimilarity) — very small on its own scale. empirical_strength = 0.995, meaning the difference is larger than ~99.5% of random re-splits. But the observed change is tiny in absolute terms.

Screening: 89 units tested, 0.44 items expected without change. One item observed. Per instructions: "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks."

So: 1 item vs 0.44 expected — same order. Therefore: Insufficient evidence.

The behavioural description: In the later window, the routing from A26 is even more concentrated on A27 (about 97.5 in 100 outgoing transitions vs about 95 in 100 earlier). The rare alternative destinations differ between windows: before, small numbers of transitions went to A08 (about 5 of 201), A20 (about 2), and single transitions to A01, A04, A06; after, single/rare transitions go to A02 (about 2), and one each to A31, A40, A45. The overall size of the difference is very small (cosine dissimilarity ~0.0005), though it is larger than in about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled data.

Important caveats: DIR shares are over outgoing transitions, not cases. Rare transitions are based on 1–5 observations each, so their appearance/disappearance is weak evidence — a rare variant can appear in one window only. The dominant route A26 → A27 is essentially unchanged.

Inference: Insufficient evidence. The evidence is insufficient to infer a structural change. One item when ~0.44 expected without change is what an unchanged process typically produces. Limitation: the single directional item concerns only rare alternative transitions from A26 and cannot rule out sampling differences in rare-variant frequencies.

- The rare alternative destinations differ between windows: earlier, A26 transitions occasionally went to A08 (about 5 of 201 transitions), A20 (about 2), and once each to A01, A04 and A06; in the later window, no transitions to these were observed, while rare transitions went to A02 (about 2 of 202) and once each to A31, A40 and A45. [DIR001]
- The overall size of the routing difference is very small (cosine dissimilarity about 0.0005), although it exceeds about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled data. [DIR001]
- These rare shares rest on only one or a few observations each (201 outgoing transitions before, 202 after), so single transitions can appear in one window only. [DIR001]

Support level: Insufficient evidence
The evidence is insufficient to infer a structural change in the process. That's two sentences after the first — the limitation sentence plus the explanation. "You may add one short sentence on the limitation." I'll keep it to one sentence ideally. Combine: "The single item matches what an unchanged process typically produces (one item found where about 0.44 are expected), and the differences involve rare transitions seen only once or twice, which sampling variation can explain." That's one sentence. Good.

Also note: "Do not speculate..." fine. "Do not discuss time or resources" — no TWAIT/ASSIGN/HAND items, so skip.

Cosine dissimilarity 0.00053 — "about 0.0005". Empirical strength 0.995 → "larger than in about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits" or "about 995 in 1000". I'll say "about 99.5 in 100".

Support counts: 201 before, 202 after — these are outgoing transitions of A26, not cases.

One nuance: the instruction says an empty profile or unobserved edge doesn't show absence. The rare destinations A01, A04, A06, A08, A20 not appearing in the after window doesn't mean those edges are gone — I should phrase as "no longer observed" rather than "removed". Good.

Also the first line of Inference must be exactly "Support level: Insufficient evidence".

It's a judgement, not a fact about data; the following paragraph has the citation.
